title: Risk, Impulse, and the Conscious Decision: Transforming Drive into Choice
summary: The adolescent seeks reward (dopamine) — risk, novelty, friends. The prefrontal cortex (the brakes) is not yet fully developed. He is not "reckless," but his brain demands reward. The strategy: (1) Provide safe alternatives for risk (adventure sports, intellectual challenge, leading a project). (2) Teach "stop-think-decide": pause for 10 seconds, think of the consequences, decide. (3) Give real decision-making space (clothes, free time, friendships) within clear boundaries.
try_this: This week: When a risk is requested, apply together: stop for 10 seconds → think: what happens if? → decide. Record: how many times did he succeed in stopping?
reflection_prompts: How many times did you use "stop-think-decide"?
Did he feel more in control?

review_defects.why: The Arabic uses 'توقف' (stop) which is a firm command, while the English softens it to 'pause'. This is inconsistent with the technique's name 'stop-think-decide' and changes the nuance of the instruction.

review_defects.english: How many times did you use "stop-think-decide"?
review_defects.why: The Arabic verb 'استخدم' is in the masculine singular form and, in context, refers to the adolescent (as in the preceding 'try_this' sentence). The English changes the subject to 'you' (the parent), altering the focus of the reflection from the child's behavior to the parent's.
